95488.e: People in the canton of Neuchâtel speak French. It belongs to Romandy, the French-speaking part of Switzerland.

95489.q: On which large lake does the town of Neuchâtel lie?
95489.e: The town of Neuchâtel lies on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel. In good weather you can see as far as the Alps from the lake.

95490.q: Which three colours are on the coat of arms of the canton of Neuchâtel?
95490.e: The Neuchâtel coat of arms has three vertical stripes in green, white and red. At the top of the red stripe there is a small white cross.
95490.m: Neuchâtel wears green, white and red.

95491.q: What is the name of the huge rock amphitheatre in the canton of Neuchâtel where you often see ibex?
95491.e: The Creux du Van is an enormous rock bowl with almost vertical walls. Ibex and chamois live there.
95491.m: The Creux du Van is a huge rock amphitheatre.

95492.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Neuchâtel border?
95492.e: The canton of Neuchâtel lies in the Jura and borders France to the west. Part of the border is formed by the river Doubs.
95492.m: Neuchâtel is a neighbour of France.

95493.q: Which big festival does the town of Neuchâtel celebrate every year at the end of September?
a: The Fête des Vendanges (grape harvest festival)
95493.e: At the Fête des Vendanges, Neuchâtel celebrates the end of the grape harvest. There is a big parade with decorated floats and lots of music.
95493.m: At the end of September, Neuchâtel celebrates the Fête des Vendanges.

95494.q: What is the name of the waterfall on the Doubs on the border between the canton of Neuchâtel and France?
95494.e: At the Saut du Doubs, the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. You can reach the waterfall by boat from Les Brenets, for example.
95494.m: At the Saut du Doubs, the Doubs leaps into the depths.

95495.q: Which world-famous architect was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel in 1887?
95495.e: Le Corbusier's real name was Charles-Édouard Jeanneret, and he grew up in La Chaux-de-Fonds. He became one of the most important architects of the 20th century.
95495.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95496.q: Which famous racing driver and car maker was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1878?
95496.e: Louis Chevrolet emigrated to the USA, where he co-founded the Chevrolet car brand. He was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds.
95496.m: Chevrolet has its roots in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95497.q: Since which year has Neuchâtel been a canton of the Swiss Confederation?
95497.e: Neuchâtel was admitted to the Confederation as a canton in 1815. At the same time, until 1848 it remained a principality of the King of Prussia.
95497.m: Neuchâtel has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

95498.q: Why is 1 March a public holiday in the canton of Neuchâtel?
a: It commemorates the founding of the Republic of Neuchâtel in 1848
It commemorates the invention of the wristwatch
The grape harvest begins on this day
95498.e: On 1 March 1848, the people of Neuchâtel declared a republic. The canton has celebrated this day every year since.
95498.m: On 1 March, Neuchâtel celebrates its republic.

95499.q: Which museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows clocks and watches from many centuries?
95499.e: The Musée international d'horlogerie in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows thousands of clocks and watches. There you learn how timekeeping developed.
95499.m: The International Museum of Horology is in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95500.q: What are the famous Jaquet-Droz figures displayed in the museum in Neuchâtel?
a: Automatons that can write, draw and play music
95500.e: In the 18th century, Pierre Jaquet-Droz and his assistants built three mechanical dolls: the Writer, the Draughtsman and the Musician. They still work today.
95500.m: The Jaquet-Droz automatons write, draw and play music.

95501.q: Which river has carved a wild gorge in the canton of Neuchâtel, with a popular footpath running through it?
95501.e: The Areuse flows from the Val-de-Travers to Lake Neuchâtel. In the Gorges de l'Areuse, paths lead over bridges and along rock walls.
95501.m: The Areuse flows through a wild gorge.

95502.q: Which two lakes is Lake Neuchâtel connected to by canals?
a: Lake Geneva and Lac de Joux
95502.e: Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten together form the Three Lakes Region. Canals link the three lakes.
95502.m: Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten form the Three Lakes Region.

95503.q: What is special about Lake Neuchâtel?
a: It is the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland
It is the deepest lake in Europe
It freezes over completely every winter
95503.e: Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but parts of them lie abroad. Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake that lies completely on Swiss soil.
95503.m: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest purely Swiss lake.

95504.q: An era of the Celtic Iron Age is named after a site on Lake Neuchâtel. What is it called?
95504.e: At La Tène, at the eastern end of Lake Neuchâtel, many Celtic weapons and tools were found in the 19th century. The later Iron Age is named the La Tène period after this place.
95504.m: The La Tène period takes its name from Lake Neuchâtel.

95505.q: What is the large archaeology museum in Hauterive on Lake Neuchâtel called?
95505.e: The Laténium shows finds from many thousands of years, from lake dwellings to the Celts. Its name recalls the site of La Tène.
95505.m: At the Laténium you discover prehistory by the lake.

95506.q: What was mined in the mines of La Presta in the Val-de-Travers?
95506.e: Asphalt was mined at La Presta near Travers for a long time. Today you can visit the tunnels as a show mine.
95506.m: In the Val-de-Travers people dug for asphalt.

95507.q: Which well-known Swiss writer lived in Neuchâtel, where a centre bears his name today?
95507.e: Friedrich Dürrenmatt lived for many years in Neuchâtel, high above the lake. His former home now houses the Centre Dürrenmatt.
95507.m: Dürrenmatt lived and wrote in Neuchâtel.

95508.q: What is special about the “CabriO” cable car up the Stanserhorn in Nidwalden?
a: It has an open upper deck
95508.e: The CabriO is a cable car with two floors. On the open upper deck you ride up the Stanserhorn under the open sky.
95508.m: On the CabriO you ride up the Stanserhorn with no roof above you.

95509.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Nidwalden?
95509.e: People in Nidwalden speak German, and in everyday life the Nidwalden dialect. The canton lies in Central Switzerland.

95510.q: Which lake is the canton of Nidwalden on?
95510.e: Nidwalden lies on the southern shore of Lake Lucerne. Places such as Hergiswil, Buochs and Beckenried are right by the water.

95511.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of Nidwalden?
a: A white double key on a red background
A black bear on a white background
A bull's head on a yellow background
An ibex on a white background
95511.e: The coat of arms of Nidwalden shows a white double key on a red background. The key is the symbol of Saint Peter.
95511.m: Nidwalden has a white double key on red.

95512.q: Which traditional festival of the Alpine herders is celebrated in Nidwalden in autumn?
95512.e: At the Älplerchilbi, the Alpine herders give thanks for a good summer on the mountain pastures. There is a parade, music and funny rhymes.
95512.m: In autumn, Nidwalden celebrates the Älplerchilbi.

95513.q: What is made at the Glasi in Hergiswil in the canton of Nidwalden?
95513.e: At the Glasi Hergiswil, glass is blown by hand. Visitors can watch.

95514.q: Which mountain rises directly above the village of Stans in Nidwalden?
95514.e: The Stanserhorn towers up just behind Stans. From the summit you can see many lakes and mountains of Central Switzerland.

95515.q: What does the company Pilatus build in Stans in the canton of Nidwalden?
95515.e: Pilatus Aircraft in Stans builds planes that are sold all over the world. The company is an important employer in Nidwalden.
95515.m: Pilatus planes are built in Stans.

95516.q: Roughly how high is the Stanserhorn in Nidwalden?
95516.e: The Stanserhorn is 1,898 metres high. You can get up by an old funicular and the CabriO.
95516.m: The Stanserhorn is just under 1,900 metres high.

95517.q: Which river flows through Nidwalden and into Lake Lucerne at Buochs?
95517.e: The Engelberger Aa comes from the Engelberg valley and flows through Nidwalden. At Buochs it flows into Lake Lucerne.
95517.m: The Engelberger Aa is the main river of Nidwalden.

95518.q: Which long motorway tunnel connects Nidwalden with the canton of Uri?
95518.e: The Seelisberg Tunnel on the A2 motorway runs from Beckenried in Nidwalden to Seedorf in Uri. It is about 9 kilometres long.
95518.m: Through the Seelisberg Tunnel you drive from Nidwalden to Uri.

95519.q: Which lake does the car ferry from Beckenried in Nidwalden to Gersau in the canton of Schwyz cross?
95519.e: The car ferry links Beckenried in Nidwalden with Gersau in the canton of Schwyz. This saves a long detour around Lake Lucerne.
95519.m: The ferry goes back and forth across Lake Lucerne.

95520.q: What is the name of the skiing and hiking area above Beckenried in Nidwalden?
95520.e: An aerial cableway runs from Beckenried up to the Klewenalp. In winter people ski there, and in summer they hike with a view of the lake.

95521.q: What is the Hammetschwand Lift on the Bürgenstock in Nidwalden?
a: An outdoor lift on a steep rock face
A suspension bridge over a gorge
95521.e: The Hammetschwand Lift travels more than 150 metres up the outside of a rock face. It is considered the highest outdoor lift in Europe. At the top there is a great view of Lake Lucerne.
95521.m: On the Bürgenstock, a lift climbs up the outside of the rock face.

95522.q: With which two lands did Unterwalden, which Nidwalden was part of, form the alliance in 1291?
95522.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the three founding cantons. Their alliance of 1291 is seen as the beginning of the Swiss Confederation.
95522.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the founding cantons.

95523.q: Which railway connects Lucerne with Engelberg via Stans?
95523.e: The Zentralbahn runs from Lucerne through Nidwalden via Stans to Engelberg. Its trains run on narrow-gauge tracks.
95523.m: The Zentralbahn takes you from Lucerne via Stans to Engelberg.

95524.q: Which important treaty of the Swiss Confederates was concluded in Stans in 1481?
95524.e: In the Covenant of Stans of 1481, the Confederates reached agreement after a fierce dispute. Afterwards Fribourg and Solothurn could be admitted to the alliance.
95524.m: In 1481 the Confederates reached agreement in Stans.

95525.q: At which airfield in Nidwalden does the Pilatus company test its new aircraft?
95525.e: The Pilatus aircraft works are right next to Buochs airfield. The new aircraft take off from there on their test flights.
95525.m: Pilatus aircraft take off in Buochs.

95526.q: How many members does the canton of Nidwalden send to the Council of States?
95526.e: Nidwalden is a canton with half a cantonal vote, formerly called a half-canton. So it has only one member in the Council of States, while most other cantons have two.
95526.m: Nidwalden has one seat in the Council of States.

95527.q: Why do you travel through Nidwalden when going from Sarnen to Engelberg?
a: Engelberg belongs to Obwalden but lies separately beyond Nidwalden
Engelberg is in the canton of Uri
There is no road through Obwalden
95527.e: Engelberg is an exclave of Obwalden. The Engelberg valley is only connected to the rest of the canton of Obwalden through Nidwalden.
95527.m: Engelberg belongs to Obwalden, but the way there goes through Nidwalden.

95528.q: Which old open-air people's assembly did Nidwalden abolish in 1996?
95528.e: At the Landsgemeinde, voters voted in the open air by raising their hands. Nidwalden abolished it in 1996; since then votes have been held at the ballot box.

95529.q: What is the Hammetschwand Lift on the Bürgenstock in Nidwalden?
a: An outdoor lift on a rock face, considered the highest outdoor lift in Europe
A rack railway up Mount Pilatus
A ski lift on the Klewenalp
95529.e: The Hammetschwand Lift climbs up a rock face above Lake Lucerne. It was opened as early as 1905.
95529.m: The Hammetschwand Lift climbs the rock face high above the lake.

95530.q: What is the capital of the canton of Obwalden?
95530.e: The capital of Obwalden is Sarnen. The town lies at the northern end of Lake Sarnen.

95531.q: On which lake does Sarnen, the capital of Obwalden, lie?
95531.e: Sarnen lies on Lake Sarnen. In summer the lake is popular for swimming and rowing.

95532.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of Obwalden?
a: A key on red and white
95532.e: The coat of arms of Obwalden is red at the top and white at the bottom. On it is a double key, each part in the opposite colour.
95532.m: Obwalden: red on top, white below, with a key.

95533.q: Which high mountain with a glacier lies near Engelberg in Obwalden?
95533.e: The Titlis is over 3,200 metres high and has a glacier. There is snow up there even in summer.

95534.q: What is special about the “Rotair” cable car up the Titlis near Engelberg?
a: The cabin rotates during the ride
It is powered by muscle strength
95534.e: The Rotair cabin turns once all the way round during the ride. That way every passenger sees the mountains all around.
95534.m: In the Rotair, the cabin turns in a circle.

95535.q: What can you watch at the show dairy at Engelberg Abbey in Obwalden?
95535.e: At the Engelberg Abbey show dairy, you look through glass windows to see how milk becomes cheese. You can buy the cheese right there.
95535.m: Cheese is made at Engelberg Abbey.

95536.q: Which pass takes you from Obwalden to the Bernese Oberland?
95536.e: The Brünig Pass connects Obwalden with the Hasli valley in the Bernese Oberland. A road and a railway line cross it.
95536.m: The Brünig takes you from Obwalden to Bern.

95537.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Obwalden?
95537.e: People in Obwalden speak German, and in everyday life the Obwalden dialect. The canton belongs to Central Switzerland.

95538.q: In which gorge in Obwalden did Brother Klaus live as a hermit?
95538.e: Nicholas of Flüe withdrew to the Ranft, a gorge below Flüeli. He lived there for many years in a small cell.
95538.m: Brother Klaus lived in the Ranft.

95539.q: Which winter sports World Cup takes place in Engelberg every December?
95539.e: On the Gross-Titlis ski jump in Engelberg, the best ski jumpers in the world compete every December. Thousands of fans watch.
95539.m: In Engelberg the ski jumpers fly.

95540.q: Which monks have lived in Engelberg Abbey in Obwalden since the 12th century?
95540.e: Engelberg Abbey was founded in 1120. Since then, monks have lived there according to the Rule of Saint Benedict.

95541.q: How many municipalities does the canton of Obwalden have?
95541.e: Obwalden has seven municipalities: Sarnen, Kerns, Sachseln, Alpnach, Giswil, Lungern and Engelberg.

95542.q: In which place in Obwalden does the Pilatus Railway, the steepest cogwheel railway in the world, start?
95542.e: The Pilatus Railway runs from Alpnachstad on Lake Alpnach up Mount Pilatus. It has a gradient of up to 48 per cent.
95542.m: The steepest cogwheel railway starts in Alpnachstad.

95543.q: What is the name of the holiday and ski resort with a mountain lake high above the Melchtal in Obwalden?
95543.e: At Melchsee-Frutt, Lake Melch lies at almost 1,900 metres. In summer people hike, and in winter they ski.

95544.q: Which river connects Lake Sarnen with Lake Alpnach in Obwalden?
95544.e: The Sarner Aa flows out of Lake Sarnen through Sarnen. It flows into Lake Alpnach, part of Lake Lucerne.
95544.m: The Sarner Aa flows from Lake Sarnen to Lake Alpnach.

95545.q: What takes place every summer on the Brünig Pass between Obwalden and Bern?
95545.e: At the Brünig Schwinget, the best Swiss wrestlers from Central Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland compete. The festival is very popular.
95545.m: There is Swiss wrestling on the Brünig.

95546.q: A company from Sachseln in Obwalden builds small electric motors that have already been used on Mars. What is it called?
95546.e: The company maxon makes precision electric motors. maxon motors have been inside several of NASA's Mars rovers.
95546.m: Motors from Sachseln have driven on Mars.

95547.q: In which year did the canton of Obwalden abolish the Landsgemeinde?
95547.e: In 1998 Obwalden voted to abolish the Landsgemeinde. Since then votes have been held at the ballot box.
95547.m: Obwalden has had no Landsgemeinde since 1998.

95548.q: Which title does Brother Klaus from Obwalden, who was canonised in 1947, hold?
a: First President of the Swiss Confederation
95548.e: Niklaus von Flüe was canonised in 1947. He is regarded as the patron saint of Switzerland.
95548.m: Brother Klaus is the patron saint of Switzerland.

95549.q: Where do the names Obwalden and Nidwalden come from?
a: From their position above and below the Kernwald forest
From two brothers called Ob and Nid
From two lakes with these names
From two castles in the forest
95549.e: People used to speak of Unterwalden “ob dem Kernwald” (above the Kernwald) and “nid dem Kernwald” (below the Kernwald). The Kernwald is a forest between the two cantons.
95549.m: Above and below the Kernwald: that's where the names come from.

95550.q: How high is the Titlis near Engelberg?
95550.e: The Titlis is 3,238 metres high. On the summit there is a glacier, an ice grotto and a suspension bridge.
95550.m: The Titlis is over 3,200 metres high.

95551.q: Which railway line runs from Lucerne through Obwalden over the Brünig to Interlaken?
95551.e: The Brünig railway is run today by the Zentralbahn. On steep sections at the Brünig, the train uses a cogwheel.
95551.m: The Brünig railway links Lucerne and Interlaken.

95552.q: What is the capital of the canton of St Gallen?
95552.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: St Gallen. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament work there.
95552.m: Canton of St Gallen, capital St Gallen.

95553.q: Which town in the canton of St Gallen is called the “Town of Roses”?
95553.e: In Rapperswil on Lake Zurich, thousands of roses bloom in several gardens. That is why the town is called the “Town of Roses”.
95553.m: Rapperswil on Lake Zurich is the Town of Roses.

95554.q: Which sausage is a famous speciality from the canton of St Gallen?
95554.e: The white St Gallen bratwurst, made mainly from veal, is known all over Switzerland. Many people from St Gallen like it best with a Bürli bread roll and without mustard.
95554.m: People like to eat the St Gallen bratwurst with a Bürli roll.

95555.q: On which large lake does the St Gallen town of Rorschach lie?
95555.e: Rorschach lies on the shore of Lake Constance. In the north, the canton of St Gallen has a share of this large lake.

95556.q: Which river forms the border between the canton of St Gallen and Austria?
95556.e: The Rhine flows through the St Gallen Rhine Valley. On one side is Switzerland, on the other side Austria.
95556.m: In the Rhine Valley, the Rhine separates St Gallen from Austria.

95557.q: Which small country borders the canton of St Gallen?
95557.e: The Principality of Liechtenstein lies right next to the canton of St Gallen, on the other side of the Rhine.
95557.m: Liechtenstein is St Gallen's small neighbour.

95558.q: Which big fair takes place in the city of St Gallen every autumn?
95558.e: The OLMA is a big fair for farming and food. The animals and the piglet race are especially popular.
95558.m: In autumn it is OLMA time in St Gallen.

95559.q: Which two cantons are completely surrounded by the canton of St Gallen?
95559.e: The two Appenzells lie like an island in the middle of the canton of St Gallen. All around them is St Gallen territory.
95559.m: St Gallen surrounds the two Appenzells.

95560.q: Which lake lies between the canton of St Gallen and the canton of Glarus?
95560.e: Lake Walen lies between steep mountains. The northern shore belongs to the canton of St Gallen, and part of the southern shore to the canton of Glarus.
95560.m: Lake Walen lies between St Gallen and Glarus.

95561.q: What is the name of the mountain range with seven peaks above Lake Walen in the canton of St Gallen?
95561.e: The Churfirsten are a row of seven peaks. From Lake Walen you see their steep rock faces, and from the Toggenburg gentle meadow slopes.

95562.q: Through which valley in the canton of St Gallen does the Thur flow?
95562.e: The Thur rises in the upper Toggenburg and flows through the Toggenburg. The valley is known for hiking, skiing and its folk music.
95562.m: The Thur flows through the Toggenburg.

95563.q: Which spa resort in the canton of St Gallen is known for its warm thermal water?
95563.e: In Bad Ragaz you bathe in warm thermal water. The water comes from the nearby Tamina Gorge.
95563.m: Bad Ragaz has warm thermal water from the Tamina Gorge.

95564.q: What is the University of St Gallen (HSG) especially known for?
95564.e: The University of St Gallen is one of the best-known universities in Europe for economics and business. Students from many countries go there.
95564.m: The HSG is a university for business and economics.

95565.q: Which of these cantons does NOT border the canton of St Gallen?
95565.e: St Gallen borders Thurgau, Zurich, Schwyz, Glarus, the Grisons and the two Appenzells. Lucerne lies further west.
95565.m: St Gallen has seven neighbouring cantons, and Lucerne is not one of them.

95566.q: Which skiing and hiking area in the canton of St Gallen lies high above Lake Walen?
95566.e: Flumserberg lies on the south side above Lake Walen. From there you look straight across at the Churfirsten.
95566.m: From Flumserberg you look out over Lake Walen and the Churfirsten.

95567.q: Which square in the city of St Gallen is covered with a red surface and looks like a huge open-air living room?
95567.e: The City Lounge in the Bleicheli district is covered with red plastic, even the benches and a table. The artist Pipilotti Rist helped to design it.
95567.m: The City Lounge in St Gallen is a red living room under the open sky.

95568.q: What is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of St Gallen?
a: A white bundle of rods with an axe on a green background
A black bear on a yellow background
A key on a red background
A white cross on a blue background
95568.e: The coat of arms shows a bundle of rods, known as fasces, on a green background. It stands for the unity of the different areas that were joined together to form the canton in 1803.
95568.m: St Gallen: green coat of arms with a bundle of rods.

95569.q: Which mountain is the highest point in the canton of St Gallen?
95569.e: The Ringelspitz is 3,247 metres high and lies on the border with the Grisons. The better-known Säntis, at 2,502 metres, is much lower.
95569.m: The Ringelspitz is St Gallen's highest peak.

95570.q: Which municipality is the second largest in the canton of St Gallen after the city of St Gallen?
95570.e: Rapperswil and Jona merged into one municipality in 2007. Since then Rapperswil-Jona has been the second largest municipality in the canton.

95571.q: Which famous reformer was born in Wildhaus in the Toggenburg in 1484?
95571.e: Huldrych Zwingli was born in Wildhaus. Later, in Zurich, he became the most important reformer of German-speaking Switzerland.

95572.q: By what name is Joachim von Watt, the St Gallen doctor, scholar and mayor who introduced the Reformation in St Gallen, known?
95572.e: Joachim von Watt called himself Vadianus in Latin, or Vadian for short. A monument in the city of St Gallen commemorates him.
95572.m: Vadian brought the Reformation to St Gallen.

95573.q: Which football club from the canton of St Gallen was founded in 1879 and is considered the oldest football club in Switzerland that still exists?
95573.e: FC St. Gallen was founded in 1879. This makes it the oldest football club in Switzerland that still plays today.
95573.m: FC St. Gallen has been playing since 1879.

95574.q: What is the capital of the canton of Schaffhausen?
95574.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Schaffhausen. The town lies right on the Rhine.

95575.q: Which neighbouring country surrounds the canton of Schaffhausen on almost all sides?
95575.e: The canton of Schaffhausen is almost completely surrounded by Germany. Only in the south does it border the cantons of Zurich and Thurgau.
95575.m: Schaffhausen is surrounded by Germany almost everywhere.

95576.q: On which river does the town of Schaffhausen lie?
95576.e: The town of Schaffhausen lies on the Rhine. In the past, boats had to unload their goods here because the Rhine Falls blocked the way further downstream.

95577.q: Which little town in the canton of Schaffhausen is famous for its colourfully painted house fronts?
95577.e: In the old town of Stein am Rhein, many houses are painted with colourful pictures. The little town is one of the most beautiful in Switzerland.
95577.m: Stein am Rhein has painted houses.

95578.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
95578.e: On the Schaffhausen coat of arms, a black ram leaps on a yellow background. The ram (in German Schafbock) suits the name “Schaffhausen”.
95578.m: Schaffhausen has a ram on its coat of arms.

95579.q: What is a “Bölletünne”, a speciality from Schaffhausen?
95579.e: In the local dialect, “Bölle” means onion and “Tünne” is a flat tart. So the Bölletünne is a tasty onion tart.

95580.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Schaffhausen?
95580.e: People in the canton of Schaffhausen speak German, and in everyday life mostly the Schaffhausen dialect.

95581.q: As far as which lake can you travel by boat on the Rhine from Schaffhausen?
95581.e: From Schaffhausen, boats travel up the Rhine via Stein am Rhein to the Untersee, part of Lake Constance. The trip is considered one of the most beautiful river journeys in Europe.
95581.m: From Schaffhausen you can take a boat to Lake Constance.

95582.q: What is special about the location of the canton of Schaffhausen?
a: Most of it lies north of the Rhine
It lies entirely in the Alps
It has no border with another country
95582.e: Almost the whole canton of Schaffhausen lies on the northern side of the Rhine. That is unusual in Switzerland.
95582.m: Schaffhausen lies almost entirely north of the Rhine.

95583.q: At what time does the little Munot bell in Schaffhausen ring every evening?
95583.e: Every evening at 9 pm, the little bell on the Munot rings. In the past it was a sign that the town gates were being closed.
95583.m: The little Munot bell rings at nine in the evening.

95584.q: In which year did Schaffhausen join the Swiss Confederation?
95584.e: Schaffhausen became a member of the Confederation in 1501. Basel joined in the same year.

95585.q: Which two Swiss cantons does the canton of Schaffhausen border?
95585.e: Schaffhausen has only two neighbouring cantons: Zurich and Thurgau. All its other borders are with Germany.
95585.m: Schaffhausen's neighbouring cantons are Zurich and Thurgau.

95586.q: In which Schaffhausen municipality is the Rhine Falls?
95586.e: The Rhine Falls is at Neuhausen am Rheinfall, right next to the town of Schaffhausen. The other bank, with Laufen Castle, belongs to the canton of Zurich.
95586.m: The Rhine Falls is at Neuhausen.

95587.q: Which well-known watch brand has its headquarters in the town of Schaffhausen?
95587.e: The watch company IWC was founded in Schaffhausen in 1868 by an American. It still makes expensive watches there today.

95588.q: What is the name of the wooded hill area of Jura limestone in the canton of Schaffhausen?
95588.e: The Randen is an outlier of the Jura in the canton of Schaffhausen. It is a popular hiking area with lookout towers.
95588.m: The Randen is the Schaffhausen Jura.

95589.q: How many separate parts does the canton of Schaffhausen consist of?
95589.e: The canton consists of a large main part, the area around Stein am Rhein in the east and the area of Rüdlingen and Buchberg in the south. German or Zurich territory lies in between.
95589.m: Schaffhausen consists of three separate parts.

95590.q: Which German village lies as an exclave in the middle of Switzerland, very close to Schaffhausen?
95590.e: Büsingen belongs to Germany but is completely surrounded by Swiss territory. People there often pay in francs.
95590.m: Büsingen is a German village in Switzerland.

95591.q: Which large industrial company, known for piping systems, was founded in Schaffhausen?
95591.e: Georg Fischer, or GF for short, comes from Schaffhausen and still has its headquarters there. The company operates worldwide.
95591.m: Georg Fischer is an industrial group from Schaffhausen.

95592.q: Which former monastery in the city of Schaffhausen now houses a large museum?
95592.e: The monastery of All Saints was founded in the 11th century. Today the Museum zu Allerheiligen shows art, history and nature.
95592.m: The All Saints monastery is now a museum.

95593.q: Which old bell from Schaffhausen is said to have inspired Friedrich Schiller's “Song of the Bell”?
a: The Schiller bell of All Saints Minster
95593.e: The bell from 1486 bears the Latin inscription “Vivos voco, mortuos plango, fulgura frango”. Schiller put these words at the start of his famous poem. Today you can see the bell at the Minster.
95593.m: The Schiller bell hangs in Schaffhausen.

95594.q: Which castle towers high above the little town of Stein am Rhein?
95594.e: Hohenklingen Castle stands on a hill above Stein am Rhein. From the top there is a beautiful view of the Rhine and the Untersee.
95594.m: Hohenklingen Castle stands above Stein am Rhein.

95595.q: What is the capital of the canton of Schwyz?
95595.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Schwyz. It lies at the foot of the two Mythen peaks.

95596.q: What are the two pointed mountain peaks above the town of Schwyz called?
95596.e: The Grosser Mythen and the Kleiner Mythen are the landmark of Schwyz. A steep path leads up the Grosser Mythen.
95596.m: The two Mythen stand above Schwyz.

95597.q: Which famous monastery is in the canton of Schwyz?
95597.e: The Benedictine abbey of Einsiedeln is over 1,000 years old. Many pilgrims go there every year.
95597.m: Einsiedeln Abbey is in the canton of Schwyz.

95598.q: Which world-famous pocket knife is made in the canton of Schwyz?
a: The Swiss Army Knife by Victorinox
95598.e: The company Victorinox makes red pocket knives in Ibach near Schwyz. They are sold all over the world.
95598.m: The red pocket knife comes from Schwyz.

95599.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Schwyz look like?
a: Red with a small white cross at the top left
White with a red cross in the middle
95599.e: The Schwyz coat of arms is completely red. At the top left there is a small white cross.
95599.m: Schwyz: red with a small white cross.

95600.q: Which group of cantons does Schwyz belong to, together with Uri and Unterwalden?
a: The border cantons on the Rhine
95600.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the founding cantons. According to tradition, they were the first to join together, in 1291.
95600.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the founding cantons.

95601.q: Which baked treat is a speciality from Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz?
95601.e: Einsiedler Schafböcke are honey gingerbread biscuits. They are shaped in wooden moulds, often with the picture of a ram.

95602.q: Which big reservoir lies near Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz?
95602.e: Lake Sihl was dammed about 90 years ago. Its water is used to make electricity, and in summer you can swim in it.
95602.m: Lake Sihl is the largest reservoir in Switzerland.

95603.q: Which famous figure do pilgrims honour in the abbey church of Einsiedeln?
95603.e: In the Chapel of Grace in the abbey church there is a statue of Mary with a dark face, the Black Madonna. It is the goal of many pilgrimages.
95603.m: The Black Madonna is in Einsiedeln.

95604.q: Which mountain, often called the “Queen of the Mountains”, lies partly in the canton of Schwyz?
95604.e: The Rigi lies between Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz. Its summit, Rigi Kulm, belongs to the canton of Schwyz.
95604.m: The Rigi is the Queen of the Mountains.

95605.q: What is the name of the huge cave in the Muota valley that is one of the longest cave systems in the world?
95605.e: The Hölloch in the Muota valley is more than 200 kilometres long. Researchers are still discovering new passages there.
95605.m: The Hölloch is one of the longest caves in the world.

95606.q: What are the men from the Muota valley who forecast the weather using nature called?
95606.e: The Muotatal Wetterschmöcker watch things like ants, fir cones or clouds. Twice a year they forecast the weather for the next six months.
95606.m: The Wetterschmöcker read the weather from nature.

95607.q: Which battle took place in 1315 on the border between today's cantons of Schwyz and Zug?
95607.e: At Morgarten in 1315, the Confederates defeated a Habsburg army. Afterwards Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renewed their alliance.
95607.m: The Battle of Morgarten was in 1315.

95608.q: Which animal park in the canton of Schwyz lies on the site of an old landslide?
95608.e: Goldau Animal Park lies among huge boulders that crashed down from the Rossberg in a landslide. Native animals such as deer, bears and wolves live there.
95608.m: Goldau Animal Park lies in a landslide area.

95609.q: On which lake does Pfäffikon in the canton of Schwyz lie?
95609.e: Pfäffikon lies on the southern shore of Lake Zurich in the Höfe region. So the canton of Schwyz borders several large lakes.
95609.m: Pfäffikon SZ lies on Lake Zurich.

95610.q: Which of these cantons does NOT border the canton of Schwyz?
95610.e: Schwyz borders Uri, Zug, Lucerne, Zurich, St Gallen and Glarus, among others. Bern lies much further west.
95610.m: Schwyz has many neighbours, but Bern is not one of them.

95611.q: Which village in the canton of Schwyz was buried by a huge rockslide from the Rossberg in 1806?
95611.e: In September 1806 an enormous mass of rock and earth broke away from the Rossberg and buried the village of Goldau. It is one of the best-known rockslides in Switzerland.

95612.q: Which large open-air theatre is performed in Einsiedeln on the square in front of the monastery?
95612.e: The Einsiedeln World Theatre has been performed in front of the abbey church at long intervals since 1924. Hundreds of people from the village take part.
95612.m: The World Theatre is performed in front of Einsiedeln Abbey.

95613.q: Which museum in the cantonal capital of Schwyz belongs to the Swiss National Museum?
95613.e: The Forum of Swiss History in Schwyz shows how people in Switzerland used to live. Like the National Museum in Zurich, it belongs to the Swiss National Museum.
95613.m: The Forum of Swiss History is in Schwyz.

95614.q: Which mountain is the highest point in the canton of Schwyz?
95614.e: The Bös Fulen is about 2,802 metres high and lies on the border with the canton of Glarus. The Rigi and the Mythen are much lower.
95614.m: The Bös Fulen is the highest mountain in Schwyz.

95615.q: Which hiking trail around Lake Uri, ending in Brunnen, was created in 1991 for the 700th anniversary of the Swiss Confederation?
95615.e: The Swiss Path runs from the Rütli to Brunnen. Each canton has a section of the path, and its length depends on the number of inhabitants.
95615.m: The Swiss Path runs from the Rütli to Brunnen.

95616.q: The funicular from Schwyz up to the Stoos is considered the steepest in the world. What is its maximum gradient?
95616.e: The Stoos funicular opened in 2017 and reaches a gradient of 110 per cent. The cabins rotate so that passengers always stand upright.
95616.m: The Stoos funicular manages a gradient of 110 per cent.

95617.q: What is the capital of the canton of Thurgau?
95617.e: The capital of Thurgau is Frauenfeld. It is also the largest town in the canton.
95617.m: The capital of Thurgau is Frauenfeld.

95618.q: Which river is the canton of Thurgau named after?
95618.e: The Thur flows right across the canton. Thurgau takes its name from it.
95618.m: Thurgau is named after the Thur.

95619.q: Which country lies on the other side of Lake Constance, opposite Thurgau?
95619.e: Germany lies on the other side of Lake Constance. Near Kreuzlingen, Thurgau also borders Germany directly on land.

95620.q: Which animals can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau?
95620.e: On the Thurgau coat of arms, two yellow lions stride one above the other. The background is divided diagonally into white and green.
95620.m: There are two lions on the Thurgau coat of arms.

95621.q: Which Thurgau town borders the German city of Konstanz directly?
95621.e: Kreuzlingen and Konstanz have grown together. You can walk from Switzerland into Germany.

95622.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Thurgau?
95622.e: People in Thurgau speak German, and in everyday life mostly the Thurgau dialect.

95623.q: Which of these cantons is a neighbour of the canton of Thurgau?
95623.e: Thurgau borders St Gallen, Zurich and Schaffhausen. The other cantons are far away.
95623.m: St Gallen is a neighbour of Thurgau.

95624.q: Which is the largest town in the canton of Thurgau?
95624.e: Frauenfeld is both the capital and the largest town. Kreuzlingen on Lake Constance comes a close second.
95624.m: Frauenfeld is the largest town in Thurgau.

95625.q: In which year did Thurgau become a canton of the Confederation in its own right?
95625.e: With Napoleon's Act of Mediation, Thurgau became a canton with equal rights in 1803. St Gallen, Aargau, Ticino, Vaud and the Grisons joined in the same year.
95625.m: Thurgau has been a canton since 1803.

95626.q: Which former monastery near Frauenfeld is now a place with museums, a hotel and its own farm?
95626.e: Carthusian monks used to live in the Ittingen Charterhouse. Today there is an art museum, a hotel, gardens and a farm estate.
95626.m: The Ittingen Charterhouse was a monastery and is now a cultural centre.

95627.q: Which drinks company in Arbon in the canton of Thurgau is known for its apple juice?
95627.e: The Möhl cider press in Arbon has been pressing Thurgau apples into apple juice for many decades. That suits the apple canton of Thurgau.
95627.m: Möhl in Arbon makes apple juice.

95628.q: Which big music festival takes place in Frauenfeld every summer?
95628.e: The Openair Frauenfeld is one of the biggest hip-hop festivals in Europe. It takes place on the Grosse Allmend.
95628.m: A big open-air festival happens in Frauenfeld every summer.

95629.q: From which Thurgau harbour does a car ferry cross Lake Constance to Friedrichshafen in Germany?
95629.e: The ferry links Romanshorn with Friedrichshafen. It carries people, bicycles and cars.
95629.m: The ferry goes from Romanshorn to Friedrichshafen.

95630.q: Which thin, rolled wafer biscuit comes from Gottlieben in the canton of Thurgau?
95630.e: Gottlieber Hüppen are crispy wafer rolls, often filled with chocolate or praline. Gottlieben lies on the Seerhein between Lake Constance and the Untersee.
95630.m: Gottlieber Hüppen are wafer rolls from Thurgau.

95631.q: What colours is the background of the Thurgau coat of arms?
95631.e: The Thurgau coat of arms is divided diagonally, white at the top and green at the bottom. On each part there is a yellow lion.
95631.m: Thurgau: white and green with two lions.

95632.q: Which museum in Thurgau commemorates Emperor Napoleon III, who spent part of his youth there?
95632.e: Arenenberg Castle near Salenstein stands high above the Untersee. Hortense de Beauharnais lived here with her son, the future Emperor Napoleon III.
95632.m: Napoleon III spent part of his childhood at Arenenberg.

95633.q: What is the long ridge of hills between the Untersee and the Thur valley called?
95633.e: The Seerücken stretches along the southern shore of the Untersee. It separates the Lake Constance area from the valley of the Thur.
95633.m: The Seerücken lies between the Untersee and the Thur.

95634.q: Which hill, at 991 metres, is the highest point in the canton of Thurgau?
95634.e: The Hohgrat is in the south of the canton near Fischingen. Thurgau is hilly, but it has no high mountains.
95634.m: The Hohgrat is the highest point in Thurgau.

95635.q: Which company from Arbon used to be world-famous for its lorries and embroidery machines?
95635.e: The Saurer company built embroidery machines, lorries and postbuses in Arbon. At the Saurer Museum in Arbon you can see old vehicles and machines.

95636.q: In which two places does the Thurgau cantonal parliament, the Grand Council, meet in turn?
95636.e: The Thurgau Grand Council meets in Frauenfeld in the summer half of the year and in Weinfelden in the winter half. This arrangement is unusual in Switzerland.
95636.m: The Thurgau Grand Council meets in Frauenfeld and Weinfelden.

95637.q: Which two parts of Lake Constance does the canton of Thurgau border on?
95637.e: Lake Constance consists mainly of the large Obersee and the smaller Untersee. Thurgau has a long shoreline on both parts.
95637.m: Thurgau lies on the Obersee and the Untersee.

95638.q: What is the capital of the canton of Ticino?
95638.e: Many people think of Lugano, but the capital is Bellinzona. That is also where the three famous castles stand.
95638.m: The capital of Ticino is Bellinzona, not Lugano.

95639.q: Which is the largest town in the canton of Ticino?
95639.e: Lugano on Lake Lugano is the largest town in Ticino. It is an important centre for banking, tourism and culture.
95639.m: Lugano is the largest town in Ticino.

95640.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Ticino border?
95640.e: Ticino juts southwards like a wedge and is surrounded by Italy on almost three sides.

95641.q: On which large lake does the Ticino town of Locarno lie?
95641.e: Locarno lies at the northern end of Lake Maggiore. Most of this lake belongs to Italy.

95642.q: Which fruit used to be so important in Ticino that its tree was called the “bread tree”?
95642.e: In the past, people in Ticino ate lots of chestnuts in winter, for example dried or as flour. Today hot roasted chestnuts are very popular in autumn.
95642.m: The chestnut was Ticino's bread tree.

95643.q: Where in Ticino can you see the whole of Switzerland in miniature, with models of houses, railways and mountains?
a: At the Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne
95643.e: Swissminiatur in Melide on Lake Lugano shows more than a hundred models of famous Swiss buildings. Little trains run through the park.
95643.m: In Melide, Switzerland stands in miniature.

95644.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Ticino?
95644.e: The Ticino coat of arms is divided vertically: red on the left and blue on the right.

95645.q: What nickname does Ticino have because of its warm, sunny weather?
95645.e: The sun often shines in Ticino, and it is warmer than north of the Alps. That is why even palm trees grow there.
95645.m: Ticino is the sun lounge of Switzerland.

95646.q: Which railway tunnel runs from Erstfeld in the canton of Uri to Bodio in Ticino and is the longest railway tunnel in the world?
95646.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long and opened in 2016. Trains can travel much faster from the north to Ticino through it.
95646.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long.

95647.q: In which year did Ticino become a canton of Switzerland in its own right?
95647.e: With Napoleon's Act of Mediation, Ticino became a canton in 1803. Before that, it was ruled as a subject territory by other cantons.
95647.m: Ticino has been a canton since 1803.

95648.q: Which prize is awarded for the best film at the Locarno Film Festival?
95648.e: At the Locarno Film Festival in August, films are shown in the open air on the Piazza Grande. The main prize is the Golden Leopard, in Italian “Pardo d'oro”.
95648.m: In Locarno you win the Golden Leopard.

95649.q: Which Ticino valley is known for its crystal-clear green water and the old stone bridge Ponte dei Salti?
95649.e: The Verzasca flows through a wild valley with green, very clear water. At Lavertezzo, the double-arched Ponte dei Salti spans the river.
95649.m: The Ponte dei Salti is in the Verzasca Valley.

95650.q: Which well-known pilgrimage church sits on a rock high above Locarno?
95650.e: The church of Madonna del Sasso stands on a rock above Locarno. You can walk up or take a funicular.
95650.m: The Madonna del Sasso stands above Locarno.

95651.q: Which of these cantons borders the canton of Ticino?
95651.e: Ticino has three neighbouring cantons: Valais, Uri and the Grisons. All its other borders are with Italy.
95651.m: Ticino borders Valais, Uri and the Grisons.

95652.q: Which mountain in Ticino is a UNESCO World Heritage Site because of its many fossils of marine reptiles and fish?
95652.e: On Monte San Giorgio, fossils were found from the Triassic period, when there was a sea here. The mountain has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003.
95652.m: Monte San Giorgio is a treasure trove of fossils.

95653.q: Which mountain, at 3,402 metres, is the highest point in the canton of Ticino?
95653.e: The Rheinwaldhorn, Adula in Italian, lies on the border with the Grisons. It is the highest peak in Ticino.
95653.m: The Rheinwaldhorn is Ticino's highest mountain.

95654.q: Where is the lowest point in all of Switzerland?
a: On Lake Maggiore in Ticino, at about 193 metres
On Lake Geneva, at about 372 metres
On the Rhine near Basel, at about 246 metres
On Lake Constance, at about 395 metres
95654.e: The shore of Lake Maggiore is only about 193 metres above sea level. This is the lowest point in Switzerland.
95654.m: Switzerland's lowest point is on Lake Maggiore.

95655.q: What is the hill near Ascona called, where artists and drop-outs sought a life close to nature around 1900?
95655.e: On Monte Verità there lived people who ate a vegetarian diet and spent a lot of time outdoors. Famous artists and thinkers visited the place.
95655.m: Early drop-outs lived on Monte Verità.

95656.q: Between which towns in Ticino did the seat of government move before Bellinzona became the permanent capital in 1878?
95656.e: In the 19th century, the Ticino government moved every few years between Bellinzona, Locarno and Lugano. Since 1878 Bellinzona has been the permanent capital.
95656.m: Bellinzona has been the permanent capital since 1878.

95657.q: Which railway tunnel in Ticino has linked the Bellinzona region more quickly with Lugano since 2020?
95657.e: The Ceneri base tunnel is about 15 kilometres long and opened at the end of 2020. Together with the Gotthard base tunnel, it is part of the New Rail Link through the Alps (NRLA).
95657.m: The Ceneri base tunnel completed the NRLA in 2020.

95658.q: What is the capital of the canton of Uri?
95658.e: Altdorf is the capital of Uri. The government and the cantonal parliament meet there.

95659.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Uri?
95659.e: The Uri coat of arms shows a black bull's head with a red nose ring on a yellow background. It is called the Uri bull.
95659.m: The Uri bull looks out from the Uri coat of arms.

95660.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Uri?
95660.e: People in the canton of Uri speak German, or to be precise the Uri dialect, a form of Swiss German.

95661.q: Which famous legendary hero is said to have come from Bürglen in the canton of Uri?
95661.e: According to legend, William Tell came from Bürglen. Today there is a Tell Museum there.
95661.m: According to legend, William Tell comes from Bürglen in Uri.

95662.q: Which river flows through the Reuss valley in Uri?
95662.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area and flows through the whole of Uri into Lake Uri.

95663.q: What is the part of Lake Lucerne that lies in the canton of Uri called?
95663.e: The southernmost arm of Lake Lucerne is called Lake Uri. It is surrounded by steep rock walls.
95663.m: Uri's part of the lake is called Lake Uri.

95664.q: On which famous meadow in the canton of Uri is the Rütli Oath said to have taken place?
95664.e: The Rütli lies on Lake Uri in the municipality of Seelisberg. Representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are said to have sworn their alliance there.
95664.m: The Rütli lies in Uri on Lake Uri.

95665.q: Since when has the canton of Uri been part of the Confederation?
a: Since 1291; it is a founding canton
95665.e: Together with Schwyz and Unterwalden, Uri is one of the three founding cantons. The Federal Charter dates from 1291.
95665.m: Uri has been part of it since 1291 and is a founding canton.

95666.q: How long is the Gotthard Base Tunnel, whose north portal is near Erstfeld in the canton of Uri?
95666.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel opened in 2016 and is about 57 kilometres long. It is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
95666.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long.

95667.q: Which pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of Glarus?
95667.e: The Klausen Pass leads from Altdorf through the Schächental across to Linthal in the canton of Glarus.
95667.m: The Klausen takes you from Uri to Glarus.

95668.q: Which pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of the Grisons?
95668.e: The Oberalp Pass leads from Andermatt to Disentis in the Grisons. The Glacier Express also goes over it.
95668.m: The Oberalp takes you from Uri to the Grisons.

95669.q: Which pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of Valais?
95669.e: The Furka Pass leads from the Urseren valley to the Goms in Valais. The Rhône Glacier is nearby.
95669.m: The Furka takes you from Uri to Valais.

95670.q: Which pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of Bern?
95670.e: The Susten Pass leads from Wassen in the canton of Uri to Innertkirchen in the Bernese Oberland.
95670.m: The Susten takes you from Uri to Bern.

95671.q: In which place in Uri has Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell” been performed for many years?
95671.e: The Tellspiele Altdorf perform Schiller's drama “William Tell” in their own theatre, the Tellspielhaus.
95671.m: The Tell plays take place in Altdorf.

95672.q: Which place in the canton of Uri is today a well-known holiday and ski resort in the Urseren valley?
95672.e: Andermatt lies in the Urseren valley, where the Gotthard, Furka and Oberalp routes meet. In winter it is a popular ski resort.
95672.m: Andermatt lies in the Urseren valley in Uri.

95673.q: Which chapel on the shore of Lake Uri recalls the legend that William Tell leapt out of a boat there?
95673.e: The Tell Chapel stands at the Tellsplatte near Sisikon. According to legend, Tell saved himself there by jumping ashore.
95673.m: The Tell Chapel stands at the Tellsplatte.

95674.q: Which mountain is the highest peak lying wholly or partly in the canton of Uri?
95674.e: At about 3,630 metres, the Dammastock is the highest mountain in the canton of Uri. It lies on the border with the Valais.
95674.m: Uri's highest mountain is the Dammastock.

95675.q: In which year was the first Gotthard railway tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo opened?
95675.e: The Gotthard summit tunnel was opened in 1882. It made the journey through the Alps much faster.
95675.m: The first Gotthard railway tunnel opened in 1882.

95676.q: In which year was the Gotthard road tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo opened?
95676.e: The Gotthard road tunnel is about 17 kilometres long and was opened in 1980.
95676.m: The Gotthard road tunnel has existed since 1980.

95677.q: Which Russian general marched his army through the Schöllenen gorge in the canton of Uri in 1799?
95677.e: General Suvorov crossed the Gotthard with his troops in 1799. A large monument in the Schöllenen commemorates this.
95677.m: Suvorov marched through the Schöllenen in 1799.

95678.q: What is the famous road along the eastern shore of Lake Uri, through rocks and tunnels, called?
95678.e: The Axenstrasse links Flüelen in Uri with Brunnen in the canton of Schwyz. It is built into the steep rock.
95678.m: The Axenstrasse runs along Lake Uri.

95679.q: Which canton does Uri NOT border?
95679.e: Uri borders Schwyz, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Bern, Valais, Ticino, the Grisons and Glarus, among others, but not Lucerne.
95679.m: Uri has many neighbours, but Lucerne is not one of them.

95680.q: What is the capital of the canton of Vaud?
95680.e: Lausanne is the capital of Vaud. The city lies on a steep slope above Lake Geneva.
95680.m: The capital of Vaud is Lausanne.

95681.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Vaud?
95681.e: Vaud belongs to Romandy, the French-speaking part of Switzerland.

95682.q: On which large lake does the Vaud city of Lausanne lie?
95682.e: Lausanne lies on the northern shore of Lake Geneva. In French it is called “Lac Léman”.

95683.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Vaud?
95683.e: The Vaud coat of arms is white at the top and green at the bottom. In the white part, the words “LIBERTÉ ET PATRIE” are written in gold.

95684.q: Which famous music festival takes place every summer in the Vaud town of Montreux?
95684.e: The Montreux Jazz Festival has existed since 1967. Many world stars have performed there.

95685.q: Which famous film comedian with a bowler hat, cane and moustache lived in the canton of Vaud until his death?
95685.e: Charlie Chaplin lived for more than 20 years in Corsier-sur-Vevey on Lake Geneva. Today his house is a museum called “Chaplin's World”.
95685.m: Charlie Chaplin lived on Lake Geneva in Vaud.

95686.q: Which Swiss city is the only one with a real underground railway, a metro?
a: Lausanne in the canton of Vaud
95686.e: Lausanne has two metro lines, the m1 and the m2. The m2 climbs very steeply up the hillside.
95686.m: Switzerland's only metro runs in Lausanne.

95687.q: Which museum about the Olympic Games is in Lausanne in the canton of Vaud?
95687.e: The Olympic Museum shows torches, medals and stories from the Olympic Games. Lausanne calls itself the “Olympic Capital”.
95687.m: The Olympic Museum is in Lausanne.

95688.q: Which big food company has its headquarters in Vevey in the canton of Vaud?
95688.e: Nestlé is one of the largest food companies in the world. Its headquarters are in Vevey on Lake Geneva.
95688.m: Nestlé has its headquarters in Vevey.

95689.q: Which European football association has its headquarters in Nyon in the canton of Vaud?
95689.e: UEFA organises the Champions League and the European Championship, for example. Its headquarters are in Nyon.

95690.q: Which big winegrowers' festival takes place in Vevey only about every 20 to 25 years?
95690.e: The Fête des Vignerons honours the work of the winegrowers. The last one took place in 2019.
95690.m: The Fête des Vignerons happens only rarely in Vevey.

95691.q: Which dish with leeks, potatoes and sausage is a speciality from the canton of Vaud?
95691.e: Papet vaudois is made of leeks and potatoes and is served with a Vaud sausage.
95691.m: Papet vaudois is leeks with potatoes and sausage.

95692.q: Which Roman town was once the capital of the Helvetii and lies near today's Avenches in the canton of Vaud?
95692.e: Aventicum was an important Roman town. In Avenches you can still see the amphitheatre today.
95692.m: Aventicum was where Avenches is today.

95693.q: After Lausanne, which is the second-largest town in the canton of Vaud?
95693.e: Yverdon-les-Bains lies at the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel. The town is known for its thermal baths.
95693.m: Yverdon-les-Bains is the second-largest town in Vaud.

95694.q: In which year did Vaud become a canton of the Confederation in its own right?
95694.e: With Napoleon's Act of Mediation, Vaud became a canton with equal rights in 1803.
95694.m: Vaud has been a canton since 1803.

95695.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Vaud border?
95695.e: Vaud borders France in the west in the Jura and across Lake Geneva.
95695.m: Vaud is a neighbour of France.

95696.q: Which valley in the Vaud Jura is world-famous for its watch manufacturers?
95696.e: In the Vallée de Joux, for example in Le Brassus and Le Sentier, fine watches have been made for centuries.
95696.m: The Vallée de Joux is the valley of watches.

95697.q: What task does the “Guet” of Lausanne Cathedral still have today?
a: He calls out the hours at night
He rings the school bell every morning
He guards the cathedral treasure with a sword
95697.e: For centuries, a night watchman has called out the hours over the city from the cathedral tower every night. This tradition still exists today.
95697.m: The Guet of Lausanne calls out the hours at night.

95698.q: In which town in Vaud did an important battle of the Burgundian Wars against Charles the Bold take place in 1476?
95698.e: Near Grandson on Lake Neuchâtel, the Confederates defeated the army of Charles the Bold in 1476 and took rich booty.
95698.m: In 1476 the Confederates won at Grandson.

95699.q: Which well-known federal institute of technology is near Lausanne in the canton of Vaud?
95699.e: EPFL is the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne. It is the French-speaking sister of ETH Zurich.
95699.m: EPFL is the ETH of French-speaking Switzerland.

95700.q: Which lake in Vaud is the largest lake in the Jura?
95700.e: The Lac de Joux lies in the Vallée de Joux at over 1,000 metres. In winter it sometimes freezes over.
95700.m: The Lac de Joux is the largest lake in the Jura.

95701.q: Which English poet made Chillon Castle famous with a poem about a prisoner?
95701.e: Lord Byron wrote the poem “The Prisoner of Chillon” in 1816.

95702.q: What is the capital of the canton of Valais?
95702.e: Sion, in German Sitten, is the capital of Valais. Two castle hills tower above the old town.
95702.m: Valais has Sion as its capital.

95703.q: Which big river flows through the whole of Valais?
95703.e: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier and flows through Valais into Lake Geneva.

95704.q: Which cheese speciality, which you melt and scrape off, comes from Valais?
95704.e: For raclette, half a wheel of cheese is melted and the soft cheese is scraped off. You eat it with potatoes.

95705.q: Which languages are spoken in the canton of Valais?
95705.e: In Lower Valais people mainly speak French, and in Upper Valais German. Valais is bilingual.

95706.q: What can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Valais?
a: A bear on a yellow background
95706.e: The Valais coat of arms is divided vertically into white and red. On it are 13 stars for the former districts, called Zenden.
95706.m: Valais has 13 stars on its coat of arms.

95707.q: What is special about the Valais holiday resort of Zermatt?
a: No ordinary cars drive in the village
The village lies on a large lake
95707.e: Ordinary cars are not allowed in Zermatt. You arrive by train and get around the village in small electric vehicles.

95708.q: Which sheep with a black face and black ears comes from Valais?
95708.e: The Valais Blacknose sheep has a white, curly fleece and a black nose. It is well adapted to the mountains.
95708.m: The Blacknose sheep comes from Valais.

95709.q: Which big dogs are named after the hospice on the Great St Bernard Pass in Valais?
95709.e: On the Great St Bernard, monks used to use big dogs to help find travellers in the snow. That is where the name St Bernard comes from.
95709.m: St Bernards come from the Great St Bernard.

95710.q: Which is the highest mountain in Switzerland, located in Valais on the border with Italy?
95710.e: The Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is 4,634 metres high. It is named after General Henri Dufour.
95710.m: The Dufourspitze is the highest Swiss mountain.

95711.q: What are the Valais contests in which Hérens cows fight for the rank of queen called?
95711.e: Hérens cows like to measure their strength by pushing their heads against each other. The strongest is crowned queen.
95711.m: Valais has cow fights with Hérens cows.

95712.q: Which fruit is grown in especially large amounts in Valais and is very famous there?
95712.e: The sunny, dry Rhône valley is ideal for apricots. Valais apricots are popular all over Switzerland.
95712.m: Valais is the land of apricots.

95713.q: Which two castles stand on two hills above Sion, the capital of Valais?
95713.e: On one hill stands the fortified church of Valère, on the other the castle ruins of Tourbillon. They are the landmark of Sion.
95713.m: Valère and Tourbillon tower above Sion.

95714.q: Which railway tunnel has connected Valais with Italy since 1906?
95714.e: The Simplon Tunnel runs from Brig to Iselle in Italy. When it opened, it was the longest tunnel in the world.
95714.m: Through the Simplon you go from Brig to Italy.

95715.q: Which base tunnel has connected Valais with the canton of Bern since 2007?
95715.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel runs from Frutigen in the canton of Bern to Raron in Valais.
95715.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel connects Bern and Valais.

95716.q: Which two neighbouring countries does the canton of Valais border?
95716.e: In the south, Valais borders Italy, and in the west France.

95717.q: Which dam in the Valais is the highest gravity dam in the world?
95717.e: The Grande Dixence dam in the Val des Dix is about 285 metres high. It holds back the water purely through its enormous weight.
95717.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

95718.q: Which Valais merchant built a large palace with three towers in Brig in the 17th century?
95718.e: Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper became very rich through trade over the Simplon Pass. His Stockalper Palace is the landmark of Brig.
95718.m: The Stockalper Palace is in Brig.

95719.q: Which place in the Valais is known for its hot thermal springs at over 1,400 metres?
95719.e: In Leukerbad, hot springs bubble out of the mountain. It is one of the largest thermal spa resorts in the Alps.
95719.m: Leukerbad is the Valais thermal spa in the mountains.

95720.q: What was the name of the Roman settlement on the site of today's Martigny in the Valais?
95720.e: The Romans called the place Octodurus. In Martigny you can still see a Roman amphitheatre.
95720.m: In Roman times Martigny was called Octodurus.

95721.q: Where does the Rhone, which flows through the Valais, rise?
a: At the Rhone Glacier near the Furka Pass
At the Gotthard by Lake Lucendro
95721.e: The Rhone begins as meltwater from the Rhone Glacier in the Upper Valais, near the Furka Pass.
95721.m: The Rhone rises at the Rhone Glacier.

95722.q: What is the famous rack railway that runs from Zermatt to over 3,000 metres with a view of the Matterhorn called?
95722.e: The Gornergrat railway has run from Zermatt up to the Gornergrat since 1898. From there you can see the Matterhorn and many glaciers.
95722.m: The Gornergrat railway runs up from Zermatt.

95723.q: What is the capital of the canton of Zug?
95723.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Zug. The town lies on the shore of Lake Zug.
95723.m: The capital of Zug is also called Zug.

95724.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Zug look like?
a: White with a blue horizontal bar
Yellow with a black bull's head
95724.e: The Zug coat of arms is white with a horizontal blue bar in the middle.
95724.m: Zug has a blue bar on white.

95725.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Zug?
95725.e: People in the canton of Zug speak Swiss German. Because of the many international companies, you also often hear English.

95726.q: On which lake does the town of Zug lie?
95726.e: The town of Zug lies on the north-east shore of Lake Zug. You can see beautiful sunsets from there.

95727.q: Which second, larger lake lies next to Lake Zug in the canton of Zug?
95727.e: Lake Ägeri lies in the Ägeri valley above Zug. Oberägeri and Unterägeri lie on its shore.
95727.m: Lake Ägeri is also in the canton of Zug.

95728.q: What is the canton of Zug compared with the other cantons?
a: The canton with the most inhabitants
The canton with the highest mountains
95728.e: Zug has an area of only about 240 square kilometres. That makes it one of the smallest cantons in Switzerland.

95729.q: What is the second-largest municipality in the canton of Zug?
95729.e: Baar lies right next to the town of Zug and, after it, is the largest municipality in the canton.
95729.m: Baar is the second-largest municipality in Zug.

95730.q: Which river flows through Lake Ägeri and Lake Zug?
95730.e: The Lorze flows out of Lake Ägeri, through the Lorze gorge into Lake Zug, and leaves it again at Cham.
95730.m: The Lorze is the river of the canton of Zug.

95731.q: What are the stalactite caves near Baar in the canton of Zug, which you can visit, called?
95731.e: The Höllgrotten in the Lorze gorge are stalactite caves. There you can see glittering limestone shapes formed over thousands of years.

95732.q: Which clock tower with a colourful roof is a landmark of Zug's old town?
95732.e: The Zytturm in Zug has a blue and white tiled roof in the canton's colours. It used to be part of the town's fortifications.
95732.m: The Zytturm is the landmark of Zug.

95733.q: What is the Zug folk festival called in which people race each other with ladders and cherry baskets?
95733.e: At the Chriesisturm, participants race through the old town with a cherry ladder. It marks the start of the cherry harvest.
95733.m: At the Chriesisturm, people race each other with ladders.

95734.q: Which fish from Lake Zug is a well-known Zug speciality?
95734.e: The Rötel is a char with a reddish belly. It is caught in Lake Zug and is considered a delicacy.
95734.m: The Zuger Rötel is a fish from Lake Zug.

95735.q: Which canton does Zug NOT border?
95735.e: Zug borders Zurich, Schwyz, Lucerne and Aargau. Bern is far away.
95735.m: Zug's neighbours are Zurich, Schwyz, Lucerne and Aargau.

95736.q: What is the name of the town of Zug's local mountain, which a funicular runs up?
95736.e: A funicular runs up the Zugerberg. At the top you can hike and look far out over Lake Zug.
95736.m: The Zugerberg is Zug's local mountain.

95737.q: What is the canton of Zug especially known for, which is why many international companies have their headquarters there?
95737.e: Zug has comparatively very low taxes. That is why many big companies from all over the world have settled there.
95737.m: Low taxes attract many companies to Zug.

95738.q: Which famous battle took place in 1315 by Lake Ägeri on the border between the cantons of Zug and Schwyz?
95738.e: At Morgarten in 1315 the Confederates defeated a Habsburg army. A monument commemorates it today.
95738.m: The Battle of Morgarten was in 1315.

95739.q: How many political municipalities does the canton of Zug have?
95739.e: The canton of Zug has 11 municipalities, including Zug, Baar, Cham, Steinhausen and Menzingen.

95740.q: Which summit is the highest point in the canton of Zug?
95740.e: The Wildspitz on the Rossberg is about 1,580 metres high. It lies on the border with the canton of Schwyz.
95740.m: Zug's highest point is the Wildspitz.

95741.q: What nickname does the Zug region have, because many companies dealing with cryptocurrencies and blockchain have settled there?
95741.e: Zug calls itself “Crypto Valley” because many blockchain companies work there. The name recalls Silicon Valley in California.

95742.q: In which municipality in Zug does the Lorze flow out of Lake Zug?
95742.e: The Lorze leaves Lake Zug at Cham and then flows on towards the Reuss.
95742.m: The Lorze leaves Lake Zug at Cham.

95743.q: Which municipality in Zug lies on the eastern shore of Lake Zug, at the foot of the Rossberg?
95743.e: Walchwil lies on a sunny slope on the eastern shore of Lake Zug.
95743.m: Walchwil lies on the eastern shore of Lake Zug.

95744.q: What is the capital of the canton of Zurich?
95744.e: Zurich is the capital of the canton and the largest city in the whole of Switzerland.
95744.m: Zurich is the capital and the largest city in Switzerland.

95745.q: Which river flows out of Lake Zurich right through the city of Zurich?
95745.e: The Limmat begins where it flows out of Lake Zurich and runs through Zurich's old town.

95746.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Zurich?
95746.e: People in the canton of Zurich speak Swiss German, or more precisely Züritüütsch.

95747.q: What is the second-largest city in the canton of Zurich?
95747.e: Winterthur lies north-east of Zurich and has more than 100,000 inhabitants.
95747.m: Winterthur is the second-largest city in the canton of Zurich.

95748.q: Which big airport is in the canton of Zurich?
95748.e: Zurich Airport is the largest airport in Switzerland. It is near Kloten.
95748.m: Switzerland's largest airport is in Kloten.

95749.q: Which mountain is the local mountain of the city of Zurich?
95749.e: The Uetliberg lies on the western edge of the city. You can get up quickly by train and have a great view.
95749.m: Zurich's local mountain is the Uetliberg.

95750.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Zurich look like?
a: Divided diagonally into white and blue
95750.e: The Zurich coat of arms is divided diagonally; one half is white, the other blue.
95750.m: Zurich has a diagonally divided coat of arms in white and blue.

95751.q: Which famous meat dish with cream sauce bears the name of Zurich?
95751.e: For Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, veal is cut into thin strips and cooked in a cream sauce. It is often served with rösti.
95751.m: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes is veal in cream sauce.

95752.q: Which reformer preached in the Grossmünster in Zurich from 1519?
95752.e: Huldrych Zwingli brought the Reformation to Zurich. He was the priest at the Grossmünster.
95752.m: Zwingli was the reformer of Zurich.

95753.q: Which Zurich church has the largest church clock face in Europe?
95753.e: The tower clock of St Peter's Church has clock faces with a diameter of about 8.7 metres.
95753.m: St Peter's in Zurich has the largest clock face in Europe.

95754.q: Which famous artist designed the coloured stained-glass windows in the choir of the Fraumünster in Zurich?
95754.e: Around 1970, Marc Chagall created five glowing stained-glass windows for the Fraumünster. Many visitors come especially to see them.
95754.m: The Fraumünster windows are by Chagall.

95755.q: Which international football association has its headquarters in Zurich?
95755.e: FIFA organises the Football World Cup. Its headquarters are in Zurich.

95756.q: What is the big rainforest hall at Zurich Zoo called?
95756.e: The Masoala Hall recreates a rainforest from Madagascar. Lemurs and chameleons live there, for example.
95756.m: The Masoala rainforest grows at Zurich Zoo.

95757.q: Which big museum right next to Zurich main station shows the history of Switzerland?
95757.e: The National Museum Zurich is part of the Swiss National Museum. The building looks like a castle.
95757.m: The National Museum stands by Zurich main station.

95758.q: Which canton has the largest population in Switzerland?
95758.e: About 1.6 million people live in the canton of Zurich. That is almost a fifth of the whole Swiss population.
95758.m: Zurich is the canton with the most inhabitants.

95759.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Zurich border?
95759.e: In the north, the canton of Zurich borders Germany along the Rhine.
95759.m: Zurich borders Germany in the north.

95760.q: Which patron saints of Zurich are said in legend to have died on the site of the Wasserkirche?
95760.e: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zurich. They even appear on the city's seal.
95760.m: Felix and Regula are Zurich's patron saints.

95761.q: Which science and discovery museum with lots of experiments is in Winterthur?
95761.e: At the Technorama in Winterthur you can try out hundreds of experiments yourself to see how physics and nature work.

95762.q: What do you call a magnet that keeps its strength for a long time?
95762.e: A permanent magnet stays magnetic for a long time, even without electricity. Fridge magnets and bar magnets are permanent magnets.
95762.m: A permanent magnet keeps its strength for a long time.

95763.q: Which stone found in nature is a magnet by itself?
95763.e: Magnetite is also called lodestone. Some pieces of it attract iron by themselves.
95763.m: Magnetite is a natural magnetic stone.

95764.q: What happens if you break a bar magnet into two pieces?
a: Neither piece is a magnet any more
95764.e: Each broken piece gets a north pole and a south pole again. That makes two smaller magnets.
95764.m: A broken magnet makes two new magnets.

95765.q: What is the area around a magnet where it has an effect called?
95765.e: Around every magnet there is a magnetic field. Only inside it does iron feel the force of the magnet.
95765.m: A magnet works within its magnetic field.

95766.q: What can you get out of a heap of sand with a magnet?
95766.e: The magnet only attracts things made of iron. Glass, stones and wood stay in the sand.
95766.m: With a magnet you can fish iron out of sand.

95767.q: What happens to a magnet's force when a nail is further away?
95767.e: The further away something is, the weaker the magnet works. Very close up, the force is greatest.
95767.m: A magnet is strongest close up.

95768.q: What can make a permanent magnet weaker?
95768.e: If a magnet gets very hot, it loses some of its strength. Hard knocks can weaken it too.

95769.q: Which magnet only works when electric current flows?
95769.e: An electromagnet is a coil of wire with current flowing through it. If you switch off the current, the magnetic force is gone.

95770.q: Which colour is the north pole often marked with on school magnets?
95770.e: At school, the north pole is usually painted red. That makes it easy to tell the poles apart.
95770.m: On school magnets, the north pole is often red.

95771.q: What colour is the south pole often on school magnets?
95771.e: On many school magnets, the south pole is marked green. That way you can see at once which end is which pole.
95771.m: On school magnets, the south pole is often green.

95772.q: Which letter is the north pole of a magnet often labelled with?
95772.e: N stands for north pole. The south pole often has the letter S.
95772.m: The north pole often has an N on it.

95773.q: How many poles does a bar magnet have?
95773.e: A bar magnet has a north pole and a south pole. They are at the two ends.
95773.m: A bar magnet has two poles.

95774.q: Is there a magnet with only one single pole?
95774.e: Every magnet always has a north pole and a south pole. Nobody has ever found a magnet with only one pole.
95774.m: Every magnet always has two poles.

95775.q: Why is the north pole of a magnet called that?
a: It is always at the top
95775.e: If a magnet hangs freely, its north pole turns roughly towards the north. That is how it got its name.
95775.m: The north pole of a magnet points north.

95776.q: Where is a bar magnet strongest?
95776.e: The poles are at the ends. Most nails stick there, and almost none in the middle.
95776.m: A bar magnet is strongest at its ends.

95777.q: How do you find the north pole of a bar magnet that has no colour?
95777.e: A freely hanging magnet turns to face north and south. The end that points north is the north pole.
95777.m: A freely hanging magnet shows you its north pole.

95778.q: Does a magnet attract a wooden ball?
95778.e: Wood is not magnetic. So the wooden ball just stays where it is.
95778.m: Wood is not attracted by magnets.

95779.q: Does a magnet attract a ring made of real gold?
95779.e: Gold is a metal, but it is not magnetic. Not every metal is attracted by a magnet.

95780.q: Does a magnet attract an aluminium drinks can?
95780.e: Aluminium is not magnetic. The magnet just slides off an aluminium can.
95780.m: Aluminium is not attracted by magnets.

95781.q: What do you call things that a magnet can attract?
95781.e: Materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic. They are attracted by a magnet.
95781.m: Magnetic things are attracted by a magnet.

95782.q: Can a magnet attract a nail without touching it?
95782.e: The magnet also works across a small gap. The nail then jumps to the magnet.
95782.m: A magnet attracts even without touching.

95783.q: Which part of a magnet attracts an iron nail?
95783.e: Iron is attracted equally by the north pole and the south pole. The pole only matters between two magnets.

95784.q: What is the force with which a magnet pulls iron towards itself called?
95784.e: The magnet pulls the iron towards itself. This force is called attraction.
95784.m: A magnet pulls iron towards it by attraction.

95785.q: A paper clip is lying on a thin piece of card. You move a magnet underneath. What does the paper clip do?
95785.e: The magnetic force works through the thin card. That is why the paper clip follows the magnet.
95785.m: A magnet attracts even through thin card.

95786.q: How can you tell that two magnets are repelling each other?
95786.e: When they repel, the magnets push away from each other. You feel resistance in your hand.
95786.m: Repelling magnets push each other away.

95787.q: Two magnets are repelling each other. What can you do so that they attract?
95787.e: If you turn one magnet round, opposite poles meet. Opposite poles attract.
95787.m: Turning one round changes repulsion into attraction.

95788.q: Can a magnet repel an iron nail?
95788.e: Iron that has no magnetic force of its own is always attracted. A magnet can only repel another magnet.
95788.m: A magnet only repels other magnets.

95789.q: How can you be sure that an object is itself a magnet?
95789.e: Ordinary iron is attracted too. But only another magnet can repel.
95789.m: Only a magnet can repel a magnet.

95790.q: Several ring magnets are on a rod. Why do some of them float in the air?
95790.e: The rings are placed with like poles facing each other. The repulsion holds them in the air.

95791.q: Can you feel the repulsion even before two magnets touch?
95791.e: The magnetic force also works through the air. That is why the magnets push each other away even before they touch.

95792.q: What is the opposite of repulsion?
95792.e: With repulsion, magnets move apart. With attraction, they come together.
95792.m: Attraction is the opposite of repulsion.

95793.q: A magnetic pole repels the north pole of another magnet. Which pole is it?
95793.e: Like poles repel each other. So whatever pushes a north pole away must also be a north pole.
95793.m: Whatever repels a north pole is a north pole itself.

95794.q: Two ring magnets float one above the other. What happens if you push the top one down and let go?
95794.e: The closer the like poles get, the more strongly they repel each other. That is why the ring springs back.
95794.m: Repelling magnets bounce like a spring.

95795.q: Why does a fridge magnet stay on the fridge door?
a: The door is made of steel
95795.e: The door has a layer of sheet steel. Steel contains iron and is attracted by the magnet.
95795.m: Fridge magnets stick to the door's sheet steel.

95796.q: Why mustn't small children play with small, strong magnets?
a: The colour rubs off the magnets
95796.e: If a child swallows several small magnets, they can attract each other inside the tummy. That is dangerous, so you must go to the doctor immediately.
95796.m: Small magnets don't belong in children's hands.

95797.q: What do people often hold on the door with fridge magnets?
95797.e: A fridge magnet is not very strong. But it can hold a note or a drawing well.
95797.m: Fridge magnets hold notes in place.

95798.q: What happens if you put lots of sheets of paper under a fridge magnet?
95798.e: The sheets make the gap to the door bigger. With a bigger gap, the magnetic force is weaker.

95799.q: Does a fridge magnet stick to a steel radiator?
95799.e: Steel contains iron. That is why the magnet sticks to the radiator too.
95799.m: A magnet sticks to many things made of steel.
